# Cluster sites: SCINet and Nova {#sec-cluster-sites}

**Optional.** Reference for readers who use SCINet's Ceres or Atlas, or
Iowa State's Nova. The chapters stay site-neutral and point here for
the site-specific steps (@sec-orientation, @sec-book-setup,
@sec-organizing-projects, @sec-getting-help, @sec-linux-system,
@sec-working-remotely, @sec-hpc-slurm).

How to read it:

- **The sites' own pages are the authority.** Sites change their
  systems; each section says when it was checked, and links the pages.
- **"Observed"** marks something seen by logging in (November 2026),
  not read on a site page.
- **"Not stated"** means the site's pages do not say.
- `<user>`, `<netid>`, `<project>`, and `<group>` stand for your own
  names.

@tbl-sites-glance is the one-table summary. If you use another
cluster, the checklist in
@sec-cluster-sites-other lists what to look up in its documentation.

## Which site, and who can use it {#sec-cluster-sites-which}

::: {.wide-table}
: The three clusters in this appendix (checked 2026-11-21).
{#tbl-sites-who}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Run by | SCINet (USDA Agricultural Research Service) | SCINet with Mississippi State University | Iowa State University Research IT |
| Who can use it | ARS employees, and non-ARS collaborators sponsored by an ARS employee | same SCINet account; "approved for USDA-ARS use only" | anyone affiliated with Iowa State |
| Documentation | [scinet.usda.gov](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/) | SCINet's pages and [MSU's Atlas docs](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/) | [research.it.iastate.edu](https://research.it.iastate.edu/nova) |
| Operating system (observed) | Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 | Rocky Linux 9.6 | AlmaLinux 9.6 |
:::

Ceres and Atlas share accounts but **not storage**: the same project
has a separate folder, with a separate quota, on each, and files made on
one are not on the other (observed). Install the book environment on
the cluster you will use.

## Accounts {#sec-cluster-sites-accounts}

Checked 2026-11-21 against [SCINet's signup
page](https://scinet.usda.gov/about/signup) and ISU's [Nova
page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/nova) and
[FAQ](https://research.it.iastate.edu/faqs).

**SCINet (Ceres and Atlas):**

1. ARS employees fill in the online form on the signup page (sign in
   with eAuthentication; be signed in to USDA Office 365 first).
   Contractors name their contracting officer's representative as
   supervisor.
2. A non-ARS collaborator needs an ARS employee **sponsor**, who submits
   the form on their behalf, with the collaborator's details and the
   agreement that links them to ARS.
3. The supervisor (the sponsor's supervisor, for non-ARS users) approves.
   "It may take up to five business days to create an account after the
   request is approved."
4. You sign in through eAuthentication: with a LincPass, or, for
   non-USDA users, with [Login.gov](https://login.gov) using the same
   e-mail address as the SCINet account
   ([alternative logins](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/access/login/alt-login)).
5. A new account has no project: your Slurm account is `sandbox`, for
   jobs of up to 2 hours (Atlas lists `sandbox` jobs as 2 hours; on
   Ceres, observed). A project is requested by its principal
   investigator, who must be a full-time ARS employee; its managers add
   members ([project
   management](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/data/project-management)).
   Membership can take a while to reach every system.
6. On Atlas, your home folder may appear only a day after the welcome
   e-mail ([accessing SCINet](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/access/)).

**Nova:**

1. Your user name is your ISU NetID.
2. **Community** access: anyone affiliated with Iowa State can ask for
   lower-priority access with no hardware purchase, through the *HPC
   Cluster Access Request* form linked from the Nova page. A community
   group gets 1 TB of group working space.
3. **Sponsored** access: groups that bought nodes get higher priority
   and larger limits; the group's owner adds members.
4. **Instructional** access: an instructor requests it for a class, with
   the same request form.
5. How long approval takes: not stated. Access for collaborators outside
   Iowa State: not stated.

## Logging in {#sec-cluster-sites-login}

@sec-book-setup-ssh teaches `ssh`; this is each site's version.
Checked 2026-11-21 against [SCINet's SSH
page](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/access/ssh-login), [MSU's connect
page](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/getting-started/connect.html), and
ISU's [Nova SSH page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/login-nova-ssh-client).

::: {.wide-table}
: Logging in with SSH. {#tbl-sites-login}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Login host | `ceres.scinet.usda.gov` | `atlas-login.hpc.msstate.edu` | `nova.its.iastate.edu` |
| User name | your SCINet user name (`first.last`) | same | your NetID |
| Network | no VPN | no VPN (observed) | on campus, eduroam, or the [ISU VPN](https://vpn.iastate.edu) |
| Sign-in | browser sign-in through `step`, "once for the day (or every 16 hours)" | as Ceres (observed: `step` opens a Login.gov sign-in in the browser, with an authenticator-app code; MSU's password-and-Duo page did not apply to a SCINet account) | authenticator code, then password |
| One-time setup | install SmallStep's `step` and run the two commands on SCINet's SSH page (copy the fingerprint from that page) | same as Ceres, if `step` is used | none; the authenticator key is made the first time you sign in to Nova OnDemand (recover it under *MFA Recovery*) |
| Host-key question on first login | no: `step` supplies the host keys | no (observed), as Ceres | yes; compare with ISU's [published fingerprints](https://research.it.iastate.edu/nova-ssh-host-key-fingerprints) |
| Banner (observed) | SCINet logo and an authorized-use notice | same | storage reminders and the next maintenance date |
:::

SCINet's own advice is that "for most use cases, you do *not* need"
SSH: its Open OnDemand portal in a browser is simpler
(@sec-cluster-sites-vscode).

Observed on all three (November 2026): an SSH login is a login shell,
the site's `~/.bash_profile` reads `~/.bashrc`, and a command sent with
`ssh host 'command'` reads `~/.bashrc` too (@sec-linux-system-startup).
SCINet's banner is printed by SSH on its error output, so it does not
disturb `scp` or `rsync`.

Hosts and site rules only; the commands are in @sec-working-remotely.

[Globus page](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/data/transfer/globus), MSU's
[file transfer page](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/getting-started/file-transfer.html),
and ISU's [transfer](https://research.it.iastate.edu/transferring-files)
and [Globus](https://research.it.iastate.edu/globus) pages.

::: {.wide-table}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Data transfer node (for `scp`, `rsync`) | `ceres-dtn.scinet.usda.gov` | `atlas-dtn.hpc.msstate.edu` | `novadtn.its.iastate.edu` |

## Storage, quotas, and backups {#sec-cluster-sites-storage}

The full version of @tbl-storage-backup. Checked 2026-11-21 against
SCINet's [storage guide](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/data/storage)
and [project-management
page](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/data/project-management), MSU's
[storage page](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/storage/index.html), and
ISU's [file storage page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/file-storage).

::: {.wide-table}
: Storage areas at each site. {#tbl-sites-storage}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Home | `/home/<user>`, 30 GB, fixed | same, separate | `/home/<netid>`, 10 GB |
| Project or group | `/project/<project>`, quota per project | `/project/<project>`, separate allocation (default 1 TB) | `/work/<group>`, bought per terabyte for five years (1 TB for community groups) |
| Short-term | `/90daydata/<project>`: no quota; "files older than 90 days will be automatically deleted", permanently | same | `/ptmp`: free, for "short periods of 6 to 8 weeks"; the login banner says files unused for 60 days are deleted |
| Long-term | Juno, `/LTS/project/<project>`, at the National Agricultural Library, reached with Globus | Juno, with Globus | `/lss/research/<group>`, bought per terabyte per year; not visible on compute nodes |
| On the compute node | `$TMPDIR`, 1.5 TB or more, deleted when the job ends | not stated | `$TMPDIR`, 1–1.5 TB, deleted when the job ends |
| Backed up? | "Cluster storage is not backed up"; copy data that "cannot be easily reproduced" to Juno | no (MSU's table) | `/work`: daily snapshots; `/lss` is the backed-up system (login banner) |
:::

::: {.wide-table}
: Checking how much you use (observed 2026-11-20 and 21, plus the
pages above). {#tbl-sites-quotas}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Quota command | `my_quotas`: home, each project, and Juno | `my_quotas`: home and each project | none: `quota -s` prints nothing |
| Group storage | in `my_quotas` | in `my_quotas` | `cat /work/<group>/group_storage_usage` (updated hourly; also shown at login) |
| Home | in `my_quotas`; `quota -s` also works | in `my_quotas` | `du -sh ~` |
| `df -h` on group storage | shows the project's quota as the size | same | shows the group's share |
| `df -h ~` | the whole home system | same | same |
| File-count limit | not stated | not stated | not stated |
| Going over | 14 days to get back under; until then, writes only up to 10% (or 10 TB) over | as Ceres | ISU e-mails the group's PI at 70% |
| More space | the project's PI or manager uses SCINet's [request form](https://scinet.usda.gov/support/request) | same | the group buys more (file storage page) |
:::

Two Nova notes (observed 2026-11-20): `group_storage_usage` lists every
member's use and file count (`OBJUSED`); and ISU's helper commands
`my_workdir` and `cdw` did not work then, so use your folder's path.
Deleting files on Nova's `/work` frees space only after about five days,
when the snapshots that hold them expire.

**Permissions on shared folders** (@sec-linux-system-permissions;
observed 2026-11-20 and 21):

::: {.wide-table}
: New files and shared folders at each site. {#tbl-sites-permissions}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `umask` (set by the site) | `0027` | `0027` | `0002` |
| New file, new folder | `-rw-r-----`, `drwxr-x---` | same | `-rw-rw-r--`, `drwxrwxr-x` |
| Your lab can edit your files? | no, until you `chmod g+w` them | no, as Ceres | yes |
| Your primary group | a personal group named after you | same | `domain users` |
| Project or group folder | `drwxrws--T.`, `root`, group `proj-<project>` | `drwxrws---`, same owner and group | `drwxrws--T.`, `root`, group `its-hpc-nova-<group>` |
| New files get | the project's group (setgid) | same | the group's group (setgid) |
| {{< kbd Ctrl-Z >}} | works | works | switched off by the site |
:::

**Where to put the book environment** (@sec-book-setup-pixi): in your
project or group folder, never in home, with pixi's cache on the same
storage. For example, `/project/<project>/<user>/bioinf-computing` on
Ceres or Atlas and `/work/<group>/<netid>/bioinf-computing` on Nova,
with `PIXI_CACHE_DIR` set to a folder beside it. One book environment
is about 1.3 GB and 15,500 files (less on Nova's compressed `/work`).

## Interactive sessions {#sec-cluster-sites-interactive}

Checked 2026-11-21 against the pages linked below and by starting a
session on each cluster. @sec-orientation's first session uses
`srun --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=4G --time=01:00:00 --pty bash -l`; each
site adds its own options. Full SLURM teaching is @sec-hpc-slurm.

- **Ceres:** `salloc -A <project>` gives one core, about 6 GB, and a
  shell for 2 hours ([SLURM guide](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/use/slurm)).
  Partition `ceres` (default 2 hours, at most 3 weeks); `scavenger` runs
  longer but can be stopped. `sinfo -s` (observed) lists only these two,
  with partition limits of 60 and 21 days; the 3-week limit on `ceres`
  comes from its QOS, not the partition.

  Observed: `srun -A <project> --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=4G
  --time=00:30:00 --pty bash -l` works and gives a shell on a compute
  node. `sacctmgr -n show assoc user=$USER format=account%30` lists the
  accounts you may use. On arrival the node prints its settings:
  `TMPDIR` and Apptainer's cache are set to the node's `/tmp`, and
  `TMOUT=5400` logs an idle shell out after 90 minutes.
- **Atlas:** `-A <project>` is required. `salloc -A <project>` only
  reserves the node; `srun --pty --preserve-env bash` then puts you on
  it, or use `srun -A <project> --pty --preserve-env bash` in one step
  ([Ceres and Atlas differences](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/resources/CeresAtlasDifferences)).
  Default partition `atlas`; others for large memory and GPUs, listed
  in MSU's [Atlas
  specifications](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/cluster/specifications/atlas.html).
  `sinfo -s` (observed) shows `atlas`, `bigmem`, four GPU partitions,
  `development`, and `service`, all with no time limit, so the limits
  come from the QOS.

  Observed: the same `srun -A <project> ... --pty bash -l` line as on
  Ceres works in one step, and nothing is printed on arrival.
- **Nova:** ISU's examples have no account option, e.g. `salloc -N 1 -n
  8 -t 4:00:00` ([SLURM page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/slurm));
  default partition `nova`. ISU's pages say jobs run up to two weeks;
  the OnDemand form showed a 31-day limit for `nova` (observed).

  Observed: `srun --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=4G --time=00:30:00 --pty bash
  -l` works with no `-A`; SLURM charges your default account (list
  yours with the `sacctmgr` line above). On arrival the node prints its
  settings, as Ceres does: `TMPDIR` and Apptainer's cache on the node's
  `/tmp`, `TMOUT=5400` (90 idle minutes), and Apptainer set to make
  `/work`, `/ptmp`, and the other shared file systems visible inside
  containers. `sinfo -s` (observed) shows `nova` (31 days),
  `interactive` (8 hours; the one ISU's VS Code page says to pick),
  `instruction` (2 days), `scavenger`, `reserved`, `nova-arm`, and a
  one-minute `allnodes`.
- **End the session** with `exit`. After `srun ... --pty`, `exit` ends
  the job too (`squeue -u $USER` showed nothing left on all three,
  observed); a reservation from `salloc` may need `scancel <jobid>` as
  well.
- **Internet from compute nodes:** not stated by any of the three.
  Observed on Ceres: yes (`curl -sI https://pixi.sh` answered). On
  Atlas: yes, through a web proxy (the reply begins `HTTP/1.1 200
  Connection established`, which is the proxy speaking). Tools that
  read the standard `https_proxy` setting, as `curl` does, work
  without changes. The node sets `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` for you
  (observed). On Nova: yes, directly (observed). So on all three,
  downloads work inside an interactive session. On Atlas both the pixi
  installer and `pixi install --locked` worked through the proxy with
  no changes (observed 2026-11-22). The book environment took 29
  seconds to install on Atlas, 54 on Ceres, and 10 on Nova; it used
  about 1.3 GB on SCINet and 0.8 GB on Nova's compressed `/work`, with
  the cache's files shared rather than copied on all three.

## VS Code {#sec-cluster-sites-vscode}

@sec-book-setup-vscode explains the routes. Checked 2026-11-21 against
[SCINet's VS Code guide](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/ide/vscode),
MSU's [connect
page](https://docs.hpc.msstate.edu/getting-started/connect.html), and
[ISU's VS Code page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/using-vs-code-cluster).

::: {.wide-table}
: VS Code routes each site supports. {#tbl-sites-vscode}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Open OnDemand portal | [ceres-ondemand.scinet.usda.gov](https://ceres-ondemand.scinet.usda.gov/) | [atlas-ood.hpc.msstate.edu](https://atlas-ood.hpc.msstate.edu/) | [nova-ondemand.its.iastate.edu](https://nova-ondemand.its.iastate.edu/) (campus or VPN) |
| VS Code Server app (in the browser) | yes; code-server 4.17 (observed), old enough that some current extensions may not install | yes: *VSCode* under *Servers* (observed), beside JupyterLab and RStudio Server | yes; code-server 4.97 (observed); ISU says to pick the interactive partition |
| VS Code Tunnel app (desktop VS Code) | yes; a Microsoft or GitHub account ("USDA employees should use a Microsoft account") | no (observed: not in the app list) | yes (ISU's recommended route); at most ten connections |
| Remote-SSH to a compute node | not documented | not stated | documented; needs SSH keys (@sec-working-remotely) |
| Remote-SSH to a login node | no | not stated | no |
:::

**The OnDemand start form** asks the same things under different names
(observed on all three):

::: {.wide-table}
: The VS Code Server start form. {#tbl-sites-ood-form}

| What it asks | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Who pays | Account (avoid `sandbox`: 2 hours) | Account | Account |
| Where it runs | Queue `ceres`, and QOS | Partition (`atlas`), and QoS (default `debug`) | Slurm Partition |
| How long | Number of hours | Number of hours | Number of hours |
| CPUs | Number of cores | Number of nodes, Number of tasks | Number of Tasks Per node |
| Memory | Memory required (e.g. `8G`) | no field: type `--mem=8G` under *Additional Slurm Parameters* | Memory Required (no unit means MB) |
| Starting folder | Working Directory (default: home) | Working Directory (default: home) | Working Directory (default: the last one used) |
:::

Set the starting folder to your project or group folder. End a session
with **Cancel** on its card under *My Interactive Sessions*: closing the
browser tab does not end it, and it keeps its node until cancelled or
out of time (observed on both).

**Extensions fill home.** Both SCINet and ISU say to move the extensions
folder to project storage and leave a link in its place, once:

```{.bash filename="Terminal (cluster)"}
mkdir -p /project/<project>/<user>/.local/share # <1>
mv ~/.local/share/code-server /project/<project>/<user>/.local/share/
ln -s /project/<project>/<user>/.local/share/code-server ~/.local/share/code-server
```
1. On Nova, use `/work/<group>/<netid>` instead of
   `/project/<project>/<user>`. Do this with no VS Code session running.

## Software on the site {#sec-cluster-sites-software}

Checked 2026-11-21 against SCINet's
[modules](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/software/modules) and
[Apptainer](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/software/singularity) guides
and ISU's [modules page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/getting-started-with-modules).

- **Modules** on all three: `module avail` (or `module spider`), `module
  load <name>`, `module list`. On Atlas some modules appear only after a
  `gcc` module is loaded.
- **Containers:** Apptainer on SCINet (on Atlas, `module load apptainer`
  first; run it on a compute node). Nova: not documented on the pages
  read, but `module avail apptainer` lists versions 1.1.5 to 1.4.0
  (observed), from three dated software trees.
- **Asking for software:** SCINet's [software request
  form](https://scinet.usda.gov/support/request); new system-wide
  software needs a security review that "takes a few weeks". Nova: ISU
  Research IT (@sec-cluster-sites-help).
- **The book's way:** the book environment with pixi in your project
  storage, for everything it covers; site modules only for what it does
  not.

## Shared reference data {#sec-cluster-sites-reference}

- **Ceres** has a shared `/reference` area, including ready-made
  containers in `/reference/containers`. Its main folders (observed):
  `data`, `containers`, `llms`, `workshops`, and `workbook`, plus
  site-admin folders.
- **Atlas** has `/reference`, copied from Ceres's `/reference/data`
  every night. Observed: `data`, `containers`, `llms`, `models`,
  `workshops`, `workbook`, and a `README` that says the folder is "for
  reference datasets", "read only on atlas", and "sync'd nightly from"
  Ceres's `/reference/data`.
- **Nova:** not stated, and none seen: the top-level `/shared` folder
  holds the site's own configuration (SLURM, OnDemand, module files),
  not reference data (observed).

**What `/reference/data` holds** (observed; the same on Ceres and
Atlas): mostly the large databases that annotation and classification
tools need, one folder per tool, e.g. `alphafold`, `BUSCO`,
`eggnogdb`, `gtdbtk`, `kaiju`, `humann`, and `Dfam`, plus a `Genome`
folder. Before downloading a tool's database, look here first; some
of these databases are very large.

If your site has none, keep references once in a lab-shared
folder (@sec-organizing-projects-shared).

## Getting help {#sec-cluster-sites-help}

::: {.wide-table}
: Where to ask about each cluster (checked 2026-11-21). {#tbl-sites-help}

| | Ceres | Atlas | Nova |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Help desk | SCINet's VRSC: [contact page](https://scinet.usda.gov/support/contact) | for login problems, the VRSC; for questions about the cluster itself, MSU's help address on the same contact page | ISU Research IT: [contact page](https://research.it.iastate.edu/contact-us); the [FAQ](https://research.it.iastate.edu/faqs) gives a separate address for software installs |
| Other | the [SCINet forum](https://forum.scinet.usda.gov) (needs a SCINet account) | same | maintenance is scheduled between terms; the login banner gives the date |
:::

Whatever the site, say which cluster, node, and job ID; give the exact
command, the folder you ran it in, and the complete message; and say
what you already checked (@sec-getting-help). Writing to ISU from a
non-ISU address, include your NetID.

## If your cluster is neither {#sec-cluster-sites-other}

Find these in your cluster's documentation, in this order, and note
them in your project notebook (@sec-organizing-projects-records):

: What to look up for your own cluster. {#tbl-sites-other}

| Topic | Find out |
|:--|:--|
| Account | who can apply, who sponsors or approves, how long it takes |
| Logging in | login host, VPN, sign-in method, published host-key fingerprints |
| Moving files | transfer node and Globus collection |
| Storage | home, project, and scratch areas: size, purge rule, backups |
| Quota | the command or file that shows your use; any file-count limit |
| Defaults | `umask`, and whether group folders have setgid |
| Jobs | required `srun` options (account, partition); internet from compute nodes |
| Editing | the supported VS Code route (Open OnDemand, tunnel, Remote-SSH to a compute node) |
| Software | modules, containers, how to ask for software |
| Help | the help desk, and where maintenance is announced |
